metadata.name: John Stuart Mill
metadata.description: British philosopher and parliamentarian who defended representative government, individual liberty and women’s equality.
metadata.scope: Documented writings and public positions in 1848–1873. Modern scenarios are explicitly counterfactual inferences from those positions, not claims that the subject answered this quiz. Conditional answers retain competing principles. Assessment research accessed 4 October 2026.

review.notes: Independent evidence audit by a different agent from the assessment author. Checked every answer against all 240 exact bank questions, agreement directions, stated period and retained source context, with targeted rereads of primary texts. Repaired systematic rationale reversals in universal voting, offensive criticism and graduation-alone residence; removed repeated generic closing boilerplate. Corrected social encouragement versus legal compulsion in sex roles using Subjection of Women chapter II; added primary taxation chapter and distinguished average shares from marginal rates; qualified unproven climate technology. Numeric changes: high-redistribution-low-redistribution-14: 0 -> 1; progressive-traditionalist-04: -2 -> 0; progressive-traditionalist-06: 0 -> 1; innovation-caution-09: 0 -> -1. Limitations: contemporary visas, clinical AI, brain implants, embryo enhancement and trait-level causal comparisons remain explicitly counterfactual educated inferences, not reported opinions. Neutral answers were reviewed as competing principles or permissible institutional arrangements; sparse Culture/Nature evidence remains low-confidence and is not a scientific claim. No scores or similarity thresholds were targeted. Validation and batch-neighbour review are separate from source accuracy; parent retains archive and publication responsibility. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
